records.author: Lorenzo_Lenovo
records.text:
Hello guest57610,
Welcome to Lenovo Community
I understand that you are concerned with the ABL behavior on your Legion Pro 27UD-10.
May I know what device are you using with it?
What you’re describing (brightness stepping down after 30 to 40 minutes and not recovering on darker scenes) sounds like protection/limiting engaging under sustained HDR load rather than standard ABL.
Let’s run through some items to isolate whether this is thermal/driver behavior, tone mapping, or a unit issue.
Key checks and adjustments:
-OSD settings (monitor side)> Ensure HDR Mode is correctly set for your use case. Try toggling between TB400 HDR and the default HDR mode to compare behavior. In OLED Care, confirm any luminance protection features are truly disabled for testing: Logo/Static Protection, Auto Dimming, and Thermal Modulation. Also look for and turn off any “Smart Power”/dynamic brightness features if present. See the
user guide
. Reboot the monitor after changes. Set Peak Brightness to High/On (if available) and HDR Tone Mapping to Standard/Default.
-Connection and signal path> Test with the bundled/high‑quality cable (Lenovo cable is recommended)  DisplayPort first. If you’re running 4K at very high refresh, temporarily test at 120 Hz in HDR to see if the behavior persists. A lower refresh can reduce sustained panel load and help tell whether thermal limiting is involved. If possible, try HDMI 2.1 at 120 Hz HDR as a comparison. Also test on another PC/GPU if available.
-Windows and GPU driver settings> Update GPU driver to the latest release and Windows to the latest build. Then reinstall the Lenovo monitor driver/ICC from the support page.
-NVIDIA Control Panel/AMD Software: set output to RGB Full, 10‑bpc (if available), and disable any driver‑side dynamic contrast/brightness or “auto tone mapping” features. Avoid third‑party overlays while testing.
-Retry running the Windows HDR Calibration after resetting previous calibration data. If the “max full frame luminance” pattern only clears near extreme values (e.g., ~2560 nits in TB400), that suggests the chain (EDID/tone mapping) isn’t aligning, usually driver or OS side. Try the calibration again after the GPU driver reinstall and with G‑SYNC/FreeSync temporarily off.
-Thermal/usage factors (for diagnosis)> Ensure the rear of the monitor has good airflow, not close to walls or heat sources. As a test, set refresh to 120 Hz and cap in game frame rate for 45 to 60 minutes. If dimming does not occur or is delayed, it points to thermal/power protection. If it still occurs on lighter content immediately after a darker scene, capture a video for support.
-Firmware (when applicable) and monitor drivers are posted on our
support site
. If no firmware is posted, the unit is running production firmware .
Test, observe and update us how it goes.
Best regards,
Lorenzo_Lenovo

records.author: exhale33
records.text:
Hello everybody. I recently purchased the Legion Pro 27ud-10 monitor and it seems there are some issues with it that i cannot solve (issues that other people have reported, elsewhere over the internet). The most important (and also annoying) one is the aggressive ABL behavior. I have set the monitor to TB400 HDR mode, disabled Dolby Vision and loaded the specific HDR color profile from Lenovo's specific Windows 11 driver (the proper one, from 2025). After a fixed 35 to a maximum of 40 minutes of gaming, ABL kicks in and relegates the monitor's display to very low brightness levels.
Now this behavior happens regardless of me turning off every option in the OLED Care OSD menu (including Thermal Modulation). If a less bright scene or portion of the game comes up, the ABL is still ON. It does not properly adjust the brightness and i believe this is a firmware issue, most likely the ABL detecting the game as a static image (which obviously, it is not). I tried factory resetting the monitor, same issue. I tried calibrating its display using the Windows HDR Calibration Tool, same behavior. What's even worse, when using the HDR Calibration Tool, the second and third screen (max detail and max full frame luminance) will have me dragging the slider up to 2560 Nits in order for the cross to disappear (which, again, should not be the case, especially in TB400 mode with DV off).
My questions are: is there any way to fix this? To prevent the (overly) aggressive ABL behavior? Will this monitor receive any firmware updates, with fixes for these issues? Can the monitor even have its firmware upgraded? I am still within the return window and i would like to know if it's worth holding on to a promise or simply returning it and getting a different model (since from what i have read, so far, everyone who's using this is experiencing the same issues as i am).
Kind regards!
